title: Kilimanjaro, met on the tarmac
description: Direct from Amsterdam or Doha. You are through immigration and away before the aircraft has finished unloading.

title: Light aircraft to the short grass
description: Ninety minutes over the Rift in a chartered Caravan, landing on a strip the camp graded that morning.

title: Mobile camp, six nights
description: Six tents, exclusive use, moved twice during your stay to stay ahead of the herds. Hot water, proper beds, no generator after dark.

title: Calving season on the plains
description: Out before first light, when the cats are still moving. Births are commonplace in February; what you see around them is the reason to come.

title: Balloon over Ndutu
description: One morning aloft at dawn, weather permitting, landing to breakfast laid out on the grass.

title: Johannesburg to Maun
description: Two hours south to north, then straight onto the delta transfer without an overnight.

title: Over the panhandle
description: Twenty-five minutes at low altitude. The delta from the air is the only way to understand its scale before you are inside it.

title: Water camp, four nights
description: Raised on a permanent island, five rooms, reached by boat. Hippo at night close enough to argue with.

title: Dry camp, three nights
description: A second camp on firmer ground where the game concentrates, so the trip covers both halves of how the delta works.

title: Mokoro at eye level
description: Poled through the papyrus by a guide who grew up doing it. Silent, unhurried, and the only way to see the small things.

title: Night drive on the island
description: Permitted here in a way it is not in the national parks. Leopard, civet, and whatever the spotlight finds.

title: Lusaka to Mfuwe
description: The scheduled morning service, met airside and driven straight into the park.

title: Into the valley
description: Ninety minutes on a road that stops being a road about halfway. Game starts before the camp does.

title: Three bush camps, six nights
description: Grass and thatch, rebuilt each season, four rooms apiece. You walk between them; your luggage goes ahead.

title: Walking with an armed scout
description: Out at six with a guide and a national parks scout. Tracks, birds, and the occasional very deliberate detour.

title: Leopard after dark
description: The Luangwa holds one of the highest leopard densities in Africa, and the night drives here are the reason people return.

title: Nairobi to Nanyuki
description: Forty minutes from Wilson, with Mount Kenya off the right wing if the cloud allows.

title: Conservancy house, seven nights
description: Exclusive use. Six bedrooms, your own staff, and no fixed timetable for anything including meals.

title: Riding the plateau
description: Horses suited to whatever you actually ride, out among plains game that ignores a horse entirely.

title: Tracking rhino on foot
description: With the conservancy's own monitoring team, who know each animal individually and are working rather than performing.

title: North to the Samburu lands
description: A full day into drier country for the northern species — gerenuk, reticulated giraffe, Grevy's zebra.

title: Permits and paperwork handled
description: Gorilla permits are capped daily and sell out months ahead. Yours are secured and paid before anything else is booked.

title: Kigali direct
description: Overnight from Europe, on the ground by morning, and met before the immigration hall.

title: Two hours to the volcanoes
description: Tarmac the whole way through terraced hills, which is not what most people expect of this drive.

title: Forest-edge lodge, five nights
description: Fireplaces, proper hot water and drying rooms that matter more than they sound after a wet trek.

title: Two treks, two families
description: Groups are assigned by fitness on the morning. One hour of climbing or four; the hour with the family is the same either way.

title: Golden monkeys in the bamboo
description: A gentler morning at lower altitude, and the better of the two for photography.

title: Windhoek, then west
description: International arrival met and transferred straight to the charter terminal.

title: Private charter, coast north
description: Your own aircraft for the week. The route is flown low along the shoreline and changes daily with the fog.

title: Desert camps, eight nights
description: Three camps, none with a neighbour inside a hundred kilometres. Canvas, stone floors, and complete darkness at night.

title: Wrecks and the seal coast
description: Walked at low tide with someone who knows which hulls are which and how they got there.

title: Desert elephant in the Hoanib
description: Tracked along a dry riverbed. Not guaranteed on any given day, which is rather the point.

title: Sossusvlei before the gates open
description: A final two nights south, into the dunes at first light ahead of the day visitors.

title: Arusha to Zanzibar
description: Ninety minutes direct from the safari circuit, so the transition happens in one morning.

title: Boat across the channel
description: Twenty minutes from the beach at Muyuni. Luggage goes separately; you do not see it again until it is unpacked.

title: Island bandas, six nights
description: Twelve rooms on the whole island, thatched, open to the sea, no glass in the windows and no need for any.

title: The reef, on your own schedule
description: Snorkel straight off the beach or dive the drop-off. Green turtles are resident and entirely uninterested in you.

title: Dhow at the end of the day
description: Sailed rather than motored, out for the light, back when you feel like it.

title: London to Oslo
description: Afternoon service, connecting north the following morning rather than the same night.

title: One night in Oslo
description: A harbour hotel and a proper dinner. The alternative is arriving in Longyearbyen already tired.

title: Longyearbyen
description: Three hours to seventy-eight degrees north, over nothing at all for the last hour.

title: Expedition vessel, eight nights
description: Twelve cabins, an ice-strengthened hull, and an expedition team that outnumbers the guests two to three.

title: North until the ice stops us
description: Bears are found on the ice edge, and where that sits changes yearly. Some years it is eighty-one degrees; some years it is not.

title: Zodiacs among the walrus
description: Landings and cruises daily, weather permitting, at bird cliffs and haul-outs the larger ships cannot approach.

title: Overnight to Quito
description: Via Madrid or Amsterdam, arriving in the evening.

title: Two nights at altitude
description: Quito sits at two thousand eight hundred metres. Two nights here is about acclimatising as much as sightseeing.

title: To Baltra
description: Two and a half hours west, plus the biosecurity checks, which are thorough and worth it.

title: Sixteen-guest yacht, seven nights
description: Crewed, stabilised, with two naturalist guides. Small enough to anchor where the hundred-berth vessels are not permitted.

title: Fernandina and Isabela
description: The western islands: flightless cormorant, marine iguana in numbers, and the coldest, richest water in the archipelago.

title: In the water daily
description: Sea lions, penguins and rays, twice a day, in five millimetres of neoprene because the Humboldt is doing its work.

title: Permits and the daily levy
description: Bhutan requires a visa and a sustainable development fee for every night. Both are arranged and settled in advance.

title: Into Paro
description: One of a handful of airports where pilots are individually certified for the approach. Left-hand side, if the weather is clear.

title: Four lodges, ten nights
description: One per valley as you move east, each with hot stone baths and a view worth the drive between them.

title: Over the passes
description: The east–west highway crosses three passes above three thousand metres. Slow, spectacular, and broken up over several days.

title: Taktsang before the crowds
description: The Tiger's Nest at opening, which means leaving in the dark and having the upper galleries largely to yourself.

title: A festival, seated
description: Timed to a tsechu in the east, where the courtyards are still local rather than ticketed.
